nodes.desc: Northeastern state with competitive politics and a left-leaning tradition, Pernambuco combines the Suape port, the Recife digital hub, the popular culture of frevo and manguebeat and strong regional inequality.

nodes.name: Ceará (Brazil)
nodes.desc: Northeastern state with a semi-arid climate and strong popular religiosity, Ceará stands out for the educational management of Sobral, wind energy, the Pecém port and center-left politics, while facing criminal factions.

nodes.name: Goiás (Brazil)
nodes.desc: Central-West state, Goiás has an economy of agribusiness, mining and agro-industry, a conservative and evangelical electorate, the largest network of military-run schools in the country and the influence of Brasília in its surroundings.

nodes.name: Flanders (Belgium)
nodes.desc: Dutch-speaking region of Belgium, Flanders is the country's richest and most populous, with an export economy centered on the port of Antwerp, strong regional nationalism (N-VA, Vlaams Belang) and broad self-government in education and culture.

nodes.name: Veneto (Italy)
nodes.desc: Region of northeastern Italy, Veneto combines small export firms, a Catholic and Christian-democratic tradition, Lega autonomism and a strong Venetian identity, having voted by a wide majority in 2017 for greater fiscal autonomy.

nodes.name: Dubai (United Arab Emirates)
nodes.desc: Emirate of the United Arab Emirates ruled by the Al Maktoum family, Dubai is a city-state of trade, finance, tourism and free zones, with a majority of foreign residents without political rights and no local elections.

nodes.name: Brazil under Juscelino Kubitschek
nodes.desc: Under Juscelino Kubitschek, Brazil was a developmentalist democracy that, through its Targets Plan, industrialized the country with state planning, infrastructure and foreign capital, built Brasília and accepted inflation and debt in the name of growth.

nodes.name: Japan in the High-Growth Era
nodes.desc: Between 1955 and 1973, Japan grew far above the world average with a coordinating state (MITI and banks), large conglomerates, industrial protection and strong exports, under a democracy dominated by the Liberal Democratic Party.

nodes.name: Taiwan under the Kuomintang
nodes.desc: Under the Kuomintang, Taiwan lived under martial law and the one-party rule of Chiang Kai-shek and Chiang Ching-kuo, with land reform, export-led industrialization, state-owned firms and US support, the base of rapid growth.

nodes.name: Indonesia under Suharto
nodes.desc: Under Suharto, Indonesia combined authoritarian military rule, anticommunism, an official party (Golkar) and liberal technocrats, attracting foreign capital and growing fast, with corruption and repression at home and in East Timor.

nodes.name: Reagan's United States
nodes.desc: Under Ronald Reagan, the United States cut taxes and deregulated the economy, confronted unions, expanded military spending against the Soviet Union and gave the religious right a voice, in a competitive democracy with growing deficits.

nodes.name: Independence-Era United States
nodes.desc: Thirteen former colonies fought the Crown for independence, government by consent and natural rights, creating republics with written constitutions and elected assemblies, religious freedom in Virginia, gradual abolition in the North and the Northwest Ordinance.

nodes.name: De Gaulle's France
nodes.desc: Fifth Republic under De Gaulle: strong presidentialism, plebiscites, dirigiste planning, nuclear independence and exit from NATO command, the end of the Algerian war and the May 1968 crisis.

nodes.name: Mandela's South Africa
nodes.desc: Post-apartheid transition under Nelson Mandela: first multiracial elections, a government of national unity, the 1996 Constitution, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and moderately liberal economic policy.

nodes.name: Legionary Romania
nodes.desc: National Legionary State from September 1940 to January 1941, a government of the Iron Guard with Antonescu: mystical Orthodox nationalism, one-party rule, antisemitism, expropriations and political violence, until the Legionary rebellion.

nodes.name: Corporatist Austria
nodes.desc: The Ständestaat of Dollfuss and Schuschnigg: the 1934 civil war, dissolved parties, the Fatherland Front, professional corporations, political Catholicism, anti-Nazism and anti-socialism, until the 1938 Anschluss.

nodes.name: Primo de Rivera's Spain
nodes.desc: Primo de Rivera's dictatorship under Alfonso XIII: the 1923 coup, a suspended Constitution, the official Patriotic Union party, censorship, public works, labor corporatism, repression of Catalans and the end of the Rif War.

nodes.name: Nevada (United States)
nodes.desc: A western US state, Nevada levies no state income tax and lives on casinos, tourism and mining, with legal gambling, quick marriage and regulated prostitution in some counties.

nodes.name: Roger Douglas's New Zealand
nodes.desc: Under David Lange's Labour government and minister Roger Douglas, New Zealand privatized state firms, cut farm subsidies, opened trade and deregulated the economy, keeping democracy and its anti-nuclear policy.

nodes.name: Argentina under the Military Regime
nodes.desc: Under the National Reorganization Process junta, Argentina closed Congress, repressed the opposition through forced disappearances and liberalized the economy, until the Falklands defeat and the return of democracy.

nodes.name: Nyerere's Tanzania
nodes.desc: Under Julius Nyerere, Tanzania adopted ujamaa socialism, with a single party, nationalized banks and industries, collective villages, Swahili literacy and a non-aligned foreign policy.

nodes.name: Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Brazil
nodes.desc: With Fernando Henrique Cardoso at the Finance Ministry and then in the Presidency, Brazil stabilized its currency with the Plano Real, privatized state firms and adopted a Fiscal Responsibility Law, in a democracy that approved presidential re-election.

nodes.name: Socialist Poland
nodes.desc: The People's Republic of Poland, a Warsaw Pact one-party state under the Polish United Workers' Party, combined a planned economy with mostly private farming, a strong Catholic Church and workers' revolts, until Solidarity's victory in 1989.

nodes.name: Samora Machel's Mozambique
nodes.desc: Under Samora Machel and Frelimo, Mozambique became a one-party Marxist-Leninist state after independence: nationalisations, communal villages, literacy and free healthcare, an alliance with the USSR and a civil war against Renamo.
